628.s: Allen asks about the early parties; Williams describes twenty-five-cent house parties with piano and drums in the back rooms, and fish fries.
628.ch: Joseph Thomas band and house parties
628.q: In the house. No long parties. Piano, second room and third room. All the front is out. And that's where the thing went on at. I used to give them too.

369.t: Fish fries, rent parties and her first stage dresses and stockings
369.s: Chaperoned by her mother and brother she played fish fries and rent scuffles; she describes the cost of outfits and her first long stockings.
369.q: Yeah, I was chaperoned by my mother and my brother. We’d play for fish frys and rent scuffles. The ladies sometimes couldn’t pay their rent so they’d give a party and sell fish sandwiches for 15 cents. Chicken (sandwiches) for the same. And that’s how they made their rent payments.

226.t: Playing popular tunes on piano rolls; tips in the whorehouse
226.s: He played whatever was popular, mentions Fats Waller piano rolls, and clarifies that bands got tips but were not playing for tips.
226.ch: Depression-era Chicago: jobs, marriage, first bands
226.q: I don’t recall the titles, but it was the songs that were popular at that particular time. I’d listen to those songs. Whatever was popular at the time was what I would be trying to play – what I would play on the piano. [?] songs.

400.t: Dan Burley, skiffle piano and house rent parties
400.s: Dan Burley ran the school paper and played skiffle, boogie-woogie piano of Chicago's house rent parties where hosts raised rent money.
400.ch: Eddie South, high school and the South Side scene
400.q: Skiffel is just boogie-woogie, another word for boogie-woogie. But they was the guys that played the house rent parties. Everybody would give house rent parties all over Chicago. This is where we really get in a thing. House rent parties, people… $30 a week and you‟re paying $100 a month for rent,…

406.t: House rent parties with pianist Bill Fry
406.s: Pianist Bill Fry took him through ten or fifteen house rent parties a weekend, paid in a dollar, food and craps luck. Barefield also trucked ice at the Hammond stockyards.
406.ch: Chicago, Virginia Ravens and the northern territory bands
406.q: Well, I met Bill Fry and Bill Fry was a piano player that played by ear. And he played all the house rent parties -- we called them chittling struts then. And they played all the house rent parties on the weekend around Chicago. So he took me with him and we would play maybe 10 or 15 of these

1.t: Piano players in fish bars, speakeasies and rent parties
1.s: Danny says pianists once had the supper-club and speakeasy gigs, and Milt describes Chicago house rent parties.
1.ch: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
1.q: In my time, of course, the piano players had all the gigs. Even in a lot of the speakeasies they had a lot of the gigs. Just piano players alone. And they'd open ...(?)... what they called suppers.

382.t: A movie-house contest prize in Rankin
382.s: She sang four shows a day for a week, won a prize of under twenty dollars and a taste of show business.
382.ch: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
382.q: : Yes. But let me tell you what happened. It was a movie house in Ranken and at the end of the movie the lights would go on and I would charleston for twenty minutes and then the movie would go on again and at the end of the movie I would dance

92.t: House rent parties during the Depression
92.s: He and his mother played the rent-party circuit with Dan Grissom, and they were paid.
92.q: But also I used to play house rent parties. This was during the Depression, and we would -- my mother would play these house rent parties, I would play, and Dan Grissom. We used to go -- we used to book house rent parties, and they'd have poker games, and whatever, you know, and they'd sell home…

19.t: First house hops (rent parties) during the Depression
19.s: He describes the rent parties with soul food and bathtub liquor, and earning around fifty cents with the guitarist.
19.q: As I said before, it was during the Depression and money was very scarce, and people in the ghetto gave these parties and things, and whoever was working came. And they would sell food, what is known now as Soul Food -- it's a later term. But they'd sell things like chitlins and collard greens,…

73.t: House rent parties and the stride pianist Rock
73.s: His aunt gave rent parties with a hired stride pianist called Rock, and young Freddie moved the furniture.
73.q: I know he just came by Rock. That's his name. So, he used to come in and play. Naturally I used to have to do all the chores like moving everything back --

125.s: Before playing with bands, Thompson learned piano at house rent parties, hired to play all night for small sums.
125.ch: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
125.q: I had only played for parties, school parties and little parties that people gave at their houses, which were later on recognized as house rent parties. And I'd like to talk a little bit about that.

112.t: Playing Philadelphia house rent parties at fourteen
112.s: He describes rent parties as a living for the hosts, with pigs feet and potato salad, and the lack of anything but an ordinary piano.
112.q: So when I got to [be] about fourteen years old, I was able to play for the house rent parties. You know, the house rent parties in those days were not for fun. For the people giving the party was to make a living. Because they'd only charge you ten cents. Then a lot of people come into them, and…
